name: Title screen & menu flow
oneLiner: A title screen built on the game's own art (its name as a bold pixel logo with a glint, a tagline, PRESS START), a menu (continue, new game, options, quit), an options screen that persists (three volumes, text speed, screen shake, flashing, reduce motion, large text, high contrast, a controls page), wipe transitions into the game and a pause menu in play (resume, options, restart, quit to title). Keyboard, mouse and touch; it draws on its own overlay canvas at a readable size on phones, consumes input only while a menu is open, and skips itself under ?auto=1, ?t= and freeze=1, so autoplay and stills are untouched.
fits: any game with a title scene
notFor: games that must start playing on the first frame with no title (use only the pause menu: isTitle returns false)
remapping keys (the controls page lists the game's keys; it does not rebind them)
games whose own title is a playable scene (the menu pauses the world while it is open)

needs: the game's canvas (the menu lays its own overlay canvas over it)
isTitle(): the game's own title scene; onStart(kind) = what the old title confirm did; onQuitToTitle() = back to that scene
canPause(): where play can be paused; optional onRestart(), canContinue(), onOption(key, value), uiRects() / obstacles() in native px
update(stepMs) at the top of the fixed step, then return while busy() (the world waits); draw() at the end of every render path
while titleShown(): draw only the title background (not the old logo or PRESS START text)
provides: get(key) / options(): master, music, sfx (0-10), textSpeed (slow/normal/fast/instant), shake, flashes (full/reduced), reduceMotion, largeText, contrast, persisted in localStorage (memory fallback)
onStart / onQuitToTitle / onRestart / onOption / onQuit / onSound callbacks, synchronous from update()
skip flags: ?auto=1, ?t=<ms>, freeze=1, ?title=0 (nothing at all), ?title=1 (force on)
rect() of the open window, lastDrawn() rects for other overlays

params.label: Pause keys (keys the game does not use)

assets: none: everything is drawn in code (5x7 bitmap font, a bold logo face built from it, 7x7 icons, a pointing glove, bevelled windows)
